Drag the globe to turn it, and click to place a pin: its latitude φ is drawn along its meridian from the equator, its longitude λ along the equator from the prime meridian (Greenwich), both as angles at the centre of Earth. The coordinates of the pin are written under the controls. *Neuchâtel* brings the pin back home, and *Grid* shows or hides the parallels and meridians, every 15°.

::: {.column-page}
{{< geores sim="latlong-globe" presets="grid" >}}
:::

## What to look for

- Place the pin on the equator, then on a pole: what are their latitudes? Why can't a latitude be more than 90°?
- Move the pin along a parallel: which coordinate changes, which one stays the same?
- Find the place on the other side of the globe from Neuchâtel (its antipode): what are its coordinates?
- Why is the longitude measured from Greenwich? Could another meridian have been chosen?

## How it works

Latitude is the angle between the equator and the place, measured at the centre of Earth, north or south (0° to 90°). Longitude is the angle between the prime meridian and the meridian of the place, east or west (0° to 180°). Earth is drawn as a perfect sphere.
